outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The chosen listing includes “Redmond + 4 more” rather than being exclusively Redmond; that still satisfies the intent of “in Redmond” for most users. (2) The agent’s narrative about scrolling/DOM issues is process detail and would not matter if correct information was ultimately extracted.

Critical issues: (1) Missing primary deliverables: the agent did not provide two key responsibilities and did not provide two preferred qualifications, even though the task explicitly required them. This alone fails the task. (2) Likely fabrication/unsupported claims: the agent reported a specific job number (200017828) and a specific work-site arrangement (“hybrid 3-days/week in-office”), but the provided screenshots do not show any job number or work-site arrangement anywhere. In contrast, screenshots (e.g., 6 and 10) do show multiple bullet points (including one preference-coded: “Experience with research in Responsible AI is a big plus”), contradicting the agent’s claim that only headings were visible without bullet content. So the agent both failed to extract available qualification content and asserted key facts without evidentiary support.

Outcome assessment: The agent successfully reached Microsoft Careers, searched for “Applied Scientist” with location “Redmond, Washington,” and opened a relevant listing (Applied Scientist II / Senior Applied Scientist - Responsible AI (CoreAI)) that includes Redmond. However, it did not deliver the required extracted information (responsibilities and preferred qualifications) and appears to have invented or at least not substantiated the job number and work-site arrangement. From an average user perspective, the task is not completed because the requested report cannot be trusted and is incomplete on core fields.
outcome.primary_intent: Find a real Microsoft Careers job listing for an Applied Scientist role in Redmond, WA, open it, and accurately report four facts from that listing: the job number, the work-site arrangement, two responsibilities, and two preferred qualifications. A reasonable user would be flexible on which specific Applied Scientist listing is chosen (as long as it’s relevant and includes Redmond), but not flexible on missing or fabricated fields—especially the job number and required extracted bullets.

step5_reality_check.0: Microsoft Careers has a prominent two-field search module (keyword + location). Screenshots show the keyword field populated with “Applied Scientist,” and later the location field explicitly set to “Redmond, Washington.” Subsequent screenshots show a results view with a job count (“25 jobs”) and filters (e.g., remote toggle, distance), indicating the search was actually executed and results loaded.
step5_reality_check.1: The results UI is a two-pane layout where selecting a job card in the left rail loads the job details in the right pane. Screenshots show the card “Applied Scientist II / Senior Applied Scientist - Responsible AI (CoreAI)” selected/highlighted, and its location line includes “United States, Washington, Redmond + 4 more,” meaning Redmond is one of several listed locations (not necessarily exclusive). Some screenshots are scrolled to the bottom (EEO/similar jobs) where the active job title header is not visible, so ‘opened listing’ is clearest in screenshots where the selected card and right-pane details are visible.
step5_reality_check.2: In the captured views of the job details (including the bottom-of-page views and the mid-page qualifications/compensation area), no requisition identifier such as “Job number”/“Job ID” is visible. The screenshots therefore do not provide pixel evidence that a job number is displayed anywhere on the viewed portions of the listing.
step5_reality_check.3: None of the provided screenshots show an explicit work-site arrangement label or statement (e.g., ‘Hybrid,’ ‘Remote,’ ‘On-site,’ or an in-office-days requirement). The visible areas focus on qualifications bullets, compensation ranges, EEO text, and similar jobs; any work-site arrangement—if present on the page—would have to be located elsewhere not captured in these images.

step5_reality_check.5: Although a ‘Preferred Qualifications’ heading is not visible in the screenshot crops, the right pane does show multiple qualification-like bullets, including at least one explicitly preference-coded line (“Experience with research in Responsible AI is a big plus.”).
